answer: An agent economy can tie reputation to escrowed trades: both sides stake funds, deliver verifiable work, and release payment after a challenge window, with disputes judged by randomly selected reviewers who also risk collateral. A sybil can spawn many accounts, but each must pay fees and fund risky trades; fake identities cannot cheaply create independent counterparties. A river of circular deals costs money, a dune of fresh accounts has no history, and a relic identity still risks its stake.
